To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel approach of physical separation of calli was used to improve in vitro plant regeneration of bread wheat cultivars.

mature embryos of ten commercial Indian bread wheats can be used for efficient and reproducible plant regeneration on hormone-free medium using a simple and novel approach of physical separation of regenerable structures from non-regenerable structures during callus induction.
mature embryos can be efficiently used for the regeneration of commercial Indian bread wheats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient, simple, reproducible and relatively genotype independent protocol for in vitro plant regeneration of bread wheat cultivars.

the development of a simple, efficient and reproducible in vitro regeneration protocol using mature embryos as explants for the ten commercial Indian bread-wheat cultivars, which will be useful in wheat biotechnology.
a simple and efficient protocol for plant regeneration from mature embryos of commercial Indian bread wheats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of TDZ (0.5 mg-1) with 2,4- D (0.5-1.0 mg- 1) is the best for callus induction and regeneration, respectively.
a high frequency and efficient plant regeneration protocol has been standardized for ten commercial Indian cultivars of bread wheat using mature embryos as explants.
the combination of 1.5 mg-1 TDZ and 0.5 mg-2,4-D was the optimum for the induction of regenerable embryogenic callus from mature embryos of the commercial Indian bread wheat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of TDZ and 2, 4-D is the most efficient for plant regeneration from mature embryo in bread wheat.
mature embryos of ten Indian wheat cultivars could be efficiently used as an alternative explant for the production of large number of plants through in vitro regeneration.
mature embryo of commercial bread wheat cultivars can be used as explants for plant regeneration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single genotype-independent regeneration protocol was successfully developed for ten commercial wheat cultivars.

mature embryos can be a useful source of explants for in vitro regeneration of commercial Indian bread wheats and the protocol is simple, efficient, genotype independent and can be used for the production of transgenic plants.
the use of TDZ in combination with 2,4 D can be used for the regeneration of a wide range of wheat genotypes, which will be useful for wheat genetic transformation.
